title: Private Deploy Pre-Install Verifications: quota, IAM policy probes, DNS sanity, and GPU availability sweep
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Goal:
Implement a robust pre-install verification sweep for Private (VPC) installs that integrates with our Terraform modules and the on-prem CLI so that customers can detect common blocking issues before beginning a full deployment. This ticket covers the verifier orchestration, the set of checks, expected outputs, and acceptance criteria.

Scope of checks (non-exhaustive):
- Cloud quotas and limits: vCPU, GPUs (count and type), public IPs, load balancer quotas, subnet IP capacity. Verify both account- and region/AZ-level quotas. Provide guidance for quota increase requests.
- IAM and service principals: ensure required roles exist and policies permit required actions (compute attach/detach, LB creation, KMS decrypt/encrypt, secrets manager access). Detect IAM boundary or SCP restrictions and report minimal remediation steps.
- DNS private zone and resolution: confirm VPC-private zones exist, required records (control plane endpoint, metrics/observability endpoints) can be created, and resolver rules are present for cross-VPC lookup if needed. Validate propagation by resolving test names from a probe instance.
- GPU capacity and compatibility: query cloud provider for available GPU SKUs in target AZs, check driver compatibility matrix (NVIDIA driver vs AMI/kernel), and flag likely preemption/spot availability issues.
- Network / firewall sanity: check that required ports (SSH for bootstrap, control plane ports, healthcheck ports) are not blocked by default network ACLs/security groups.
- KMS / key material: verify KMS keys exist, key policies allow the expected service principals, and key rotation state is acceptable.

Design notes and constraints:
- The verifier should be idempotent and safe to run from both customer CI and our install operator.
- Primary implementation surface: a small Go binary (redwood-preinstall) that can be invoked as a Terraform null_resource (local-exec) or as a standalone CLI. It will use provider SDKs where possible to avoid brittle HTML scraping.
- Output: machine-readable JSON with structured results and human-readable summary. Exit codes: 0 = pass, 2 = warnings-only, 3 = blocking failures.
- Timeouts and backoff: network-calls use exponential backoff; aggregate runtime should aim for < 5 minutes in most regions.
- Configurable checks: users can opt-in/opt-out checks (e.g. skip GPU probe for CPU-only installs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module exposes a flag to run verifier during plan/apply and surfaces non-blocking warnings as notes in terraform output.
- The Go binary returns clear remediation steps for each failing check and emits a single JSON report compatible with our Console ingest (schema v1).
- Integration tests cover at least three cloud regions and simulate quota, IAM, and DNS failures via mocked provider responses.
- Documentation (Console runbook + Quickstart) published to Confluence with example outputs and a sample remediation checklist.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Automatic quota request submissions (follow-up).
- Deep per-kernel GPU performance profiling (follow-up).

Notes for implementation:
- Reuse logic from ENG-... runtime quota auditors where applicable but avoid copying CLI semantics that assume hosted environment.
- Add a small helper library that can be imported by internal install operator to reuse checks without spawning a process.
- Ensure error messages are actionable: include exact IAM policy actions to add, exact DNS records to create, or exact cloud console links for quota increase.

Links and references:
- Driver compatibility matrix: https://docs.internal.redwood/driver-matrix (placeholder)
- Example Terraform usage (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/tree/preinstall-sweeper
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Carter: Initial ticket created after customer pilot encountered quota and DNS failures during a private install. Captured scope and acceptance criteria. Requested 2-week spike to validate feasibility.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Santos: Spike results attached in PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/128). Implemented basic quota probe for AWS and GCP. Found inconsistent API shapes for GPU availability on GCE - added an adapter layer.

2026-03-05 - Design review (Elena Park): Suggest adding human-readable remediation steps and cross-link to Confluence runbook. Also recommended we add explicit check for IAM permission boundaries and org-level SCPs.
2026-03-06 - Miguel Santos: Added IAM boundary detection (checks for aws:ViaAWSService and iam:PermissionsBoundary). Updated CLI to emit recommended minimal role documents. PR #130 opened for review.

2026-03-08 - QA (Ravi Patel): Ran verifier against staging account. Caught an issue where DNS probe timed out behind a restrictive NACL; added optional jump-probe via ephemeral VM. Filing follow-up to harden timeouts (ENG-84322).

2026-03-10 - Miguel Santos: Wire-up to Terraform module done; terraform sample prints warnings and failure causes during plan (see sample output in PR). Added JSON schema v1 and Console ingest stub. Requesting code review and security review before merge.
notes: Follow-ups: ENG-84322 (timeout/backoff hardening), ENG-84323 (automatic quota request prototype). Plan to schedule security review week of 2026-03-15.
